write: a follow-up email to your three teammates after a call with a supplier
situation: You just got off a call with the company that prints your organization's quarterly magazine. Write the follow-up email to your three teammates.
notes: the price goes up 12% from the spring issue, from $4,200 to about $4,700 a run
they will hold the old price if you sign a two-year contract
turnaround drops from 10 working days to 7 either way
they need an answer by Friday the 21st
your contact there is Dana
the other quote you got last year was $5,100
you lean toward signing, but you want to hear objections first

write: a chat reply to a colleague who asked why the newsletter went out so late yesterday
situation: A colleague messages you: "why did the newsletter go out so late yesterday?" Write your reply in chat.
notes: it was scheduled for 9:00 and went out at 2:40 in the afternoon
the mailing tool refused to send because the subscriber list you imported had about 300 duplicate addresses
you only found out at 11, when someone asked where it was
cleaning the list took the rest of the time
from now on the import gets checked the day before
the open rate looks normal anyway: 41%, against the usual 43%

write: a short follow-up to all staff about an overbooked public workshop
situation: Last Thursday's public workshop was overbooked. Write the short follow-up for all staff.
notes: there were 60 seats and 78 people turned up
the sign-up form stayed open past the limit, because the limit was set on the old form and not on the copy made in March
18 people stood or left
4 people complained by email; each got an apology and a free place at the next workshop
from now on one named person owns each event's form and closes it by hand; the job rotates
the next workshop is on the 14th

genre: description of a change, for a reviewer
write: a description of a change you made, for the colleague who has to approve it
situation: You rewrote your team's "How to request time off" page. Describe the change for the colleague who has to approve it before it replaces the old page.
notes: the old page was 1,400 words; the new one is about 500
the step-by-step instructions moved to the top
the section about the paper form is gone; the paper form was retired in 2023
new: what to do when your manager is away (ask their deputy, who is listed in the staff directory)
the policy itself did not change, only the wording and the order
you were not sure whether "at least two weeks' notice" applies to single days off, so you kept the old wording
you want the reviewer to look at that part in particular

write: an email declining a request and offering alternatives
situation: A colleague in another department asked you to edit their 30-page grant report by Monday. You can't. Write your reply.
notes: you are on deadline for the annual report until Wednesday
by Monday you could read the summary and the budget narrative, about 6 pages
or you could do the whole report by the Friday after
Priya, a freelancer you trust, may have time this week
you want it to go well: the grant pays for two positions

write: a weekly status update to your manager on the website rewrite
situation: Write this week's status update to your manager on the website rewrite.
notes: 34 of 52 pages are rewritten; it was 27 last week
the About section is finished and signed off
the services pages are stuck: legal has had the pricing language for 9 days and you have chased twice
if legal has not answered by Thursday, the launch on the 30th slips by a week
the photo shoot is booked for Tuesday
you need nothing from your manager, except perhaps a nudge to legal

write: a chat reply giving a junior colleague feedback on their draft press release
situation: A junior colleague sent you the first draft of a press release and asked what you think. Reply in chat.
notes: the news, that the new community library opens on May 3, is buried in the third paragraph
the first paragraph is all background
the quote from the director is good and should stay
it runs 600 words and should be about 350
the headline is fine
the contact details at the bottom are last year's
overall it is close, and better than most first drafts

write: the opening of a short opinion piece arguing that most meeting notes are useless
situation: Write the opening of a short opinion piece for a general work audience. The argument: most meeting notes are useless. Use these points and put them your own way.
notes: notes record what was said, not what was decided
nobody reads them after two days
the useful part fits in three lines: what was decided, who does what by when, and what is still open
long notes feel diligent, which is why people keep writing them
an example: a 90-minute planning meeting produced four pages of notes, and afterward nobody could say who owned the budget

write: an email to the programs team asking them to review the new volunteer handbook
situation: You finished the new volunteer handbook and need the programs team to review it. Write the email asking them.
notes: the draft is finished and runs 22 pages
you need their review of section 3 (safeguarding) and section 5 (shift scheduling) in particular
comments go in the shared document by Wednesday the 12th
printing is booked for the 17th, so later changes cannot go in
the old handbook was last updated in 2021
you can walk anyone through the changes in 15 minutes if that is easier
you know it is a busy month for them

write: a chat reply to a teammate who asked why the office move was pushed back
situation: A teammate messages you: "why did the office move get pushed back?" Write your reply in chat.
notes: the move was planned for the weekend of the 8th and is now the weekend of the 22nd
the lift in the new building failed its inspection, and the movers will not carry desks up three floors
the re-inspection is on the 15th
if it fails again, the fallback is to move the ground-floor teams first
IT cannot move the server cabinet until the lift works either
packing crates still arrive this week, so people can start packing
you will confirm on the 16th

write: a follow-up message to everyone who attended the planning meeting, summarizing what was decided
situation: Tuesday's planning meeting ran 90 minutes with nine people. Write the follow-up to everyone who attended.
notes: the autumn campaign launches on October 6, not September 15
the budget stays at 40,000, with 6,000 moved from print ads to video
Sam owns the video brief, due on the 20th
Lena owns the mailing list cleanup, due at the end of the month
not decided: whether to hire a freelance designer; Omar gets two quotes by Friday
the next meeting is on the 27th

write: the opening of a blog post arguing that small teams should not copy big-company processes
situation: Write the opening of a blog post for people who run small teams. The argument: small teams should not copy big-company processes.
notes: big companies add process to coordinate hundreds of people who do not know each other
a team of six already knows what everyone is doing
copied process, such as weekly status reports, approval chains, and quarterly planning documents, costs the same hours and returns less
an example: a five-person shop that spent every Monday morning writing status reports nobody read
what a small team needs instead: a shared list of what is in progress, and the habit of talking
add process when something has broken twice, not before
